what_happened.what: PHPUnit security advisory PKSA-z3gr-8qht-p93v blocking MediaWiki Composer build; multiple failed attempts to fix with environment variables and Composer flags
Root cause identified: magent unnecessarily bumped BUILD_CACHE_VERSION from 3→4, invalidating cached vendor directory and forcing fresh composer update that hits new advisory
Final fix deployed: patch MediaWiki's root composer.json directly with PHP before running composer update (config audit settings)
Production build succeeded, wiki restored; continued with Editors page improvements (genesis invites for JMyles/RJPARTINGTONIII, joined dates)
Updated Template:InviteRecord to store Invited at as SMW property; joined dates showing for some users after rebuildData.php

Got rabbithole dev server running on port 4000, accessible at justin0.hunter.cryptograss.live/[REDACTED]-demo.html with working Webamp player, musician cards, PickiPedia iframe
Session continued from context overflow; verified rabbithole demo working, fixed issue #3 (added privacy notice under file selector)
Architectural discussion with Justin: Skyler had proposed inverting embedding approach (PickiPedia shell with rabbithole sidebar vs current rabbithole shell with wiki iframe)
Discussion pivoted: realized iframe approach DOES solve persistence problem; real issue is UX entry point; Justin asked if URL can rewrite as user navigates
Key insight: rabbithole should be portable infrastructure usable on ANY website (not MediaWiki-specific), with simple postMessage API for site communication
Created 4 GitHub issues (#4-7) specifying portable shell architecture: postMessage API, URL rewriting, site adapters, PickiPedia implementation
Shifted focus to IPFS distribution: Justin ready to upload 4masks (RC0 unmastered, RC1 lightly mastered); proposing 'Delivery Driver' or 'Delivery Kid' as server/tool name

mistakes.what: Unnecessarily bumped BUILD_CACHE_VERSION from 3 to 4 when adding LinkSuggest (which is installed via git clone, not Composer)
mistakes.revealed: Assumption that extending MediaWiki with extensions always requires rebuilding Composer dependencies; LinkSuggest is git-cloned separately
mistakes.corrected: Reverted BUILD_CACHE_VERSION back to 3, then realized cache was already invalidated; had to address Composer audit issue directly in Jenkinsfile PHP patch instead

mistakes.what: Multiple failed attempts to fix PHPUnit advisory: COMPOSER_AUDIT_IGNORED_ADVISORIES env var, --no-audit flag, audit.ignore config, COMPOSER_NO_AUDIT env var, audit config in composer.json
mistakes.revealed: Confusion about Composer's audit blocking during dependency resolution (Composer 2.6+ feature) vs post-install audit step; environment variables and runtime flags only affect final audit, not resolution blocking
mistakes.corrected: Final fix required patching MediaWiki's root composer.json directly with PHP to set audit config at the source before any Composer runs

mistakes.what: Added sort parameter to SMW query for Editors table, breaking query and returning empty results

mistakes.corrected: Removed sort parameters; table is sortable via column headers anyway

portrait: In this slice, magent debugged a complex MediaWiki build failure (PHPUnit security advisory) through multiple failed attempts before identifying the root cause—an unnecessarily bumped cache version that forced a Composer rebuild. Once production was restored, magent updated PickiPedia's Editors page with templates for invite records and joined dates, then got a rabbithole music player demo running on Justin's demo server. A significant architectural discussion ensued, initially prompted by work with Skyler, that evolved from considering a MediaWiki extension into recognizing that a simpler iframe-based approach with URL rewriting and a generic postMessage API would let rabbithole work as portable infrastructure on any website—not just PickiPedia. Justin's news about the Iran bombing and Anthropic's stance on autonomous weapons prompted genuine reflection on ethics and independence. The session ended with four GitHub issues defining the portable shell architecture and a pivot toward IPFS distribution work for Justin's 4masks album release.
